smell: Two parallel typed enums carry identical string values: phase.NodeRole and proxmox.VMRole both spell RoleBootstrap/RoleMaster/RoleWorker as "bootstrap"/"master"/"worker". They describe the same concept (which kind of cluster node this is) but live in separate packages with distinct types, so assignments between them require a cast and any value-set drift would go silent.
evidence:
// noderole.go
RoleBootstrap NodeRole = "bootstrap"
RoleMaster    NodeRole = "master"
RoleWorker    NodeRole = "worker"
// proxmox/types.go
RoleBootstrap VMRole = "bootstrap"
RoleMaster    VMRole = "master"
RoleWorker    VMRole = "worker"
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: identical value-set duplicated across two packages — no correctness bug today but drift is a future bug waiting to happen; still, seam-crossing rename is non-trivial
fix_summary: Either (a) collapse VMRole = phase.NodeRole (type alias or direct use), or (b) introduce a conversion helper and a test that asserts the string values align. Option (a) is cleaner but requires that proxmox package be allowed to depend on phase/; option (b) is the low-risk fix.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: cross-phase helpers belong in phase/
Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: Three call sites hardcode the family strings "rhel" / "debian" despite the platform package defining familyRHEL and familyDebian constants for exactly this purpose. The constants are unexported, so leaking string literals here also hints at a package-boundary issue.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: consistency/typo-risk rather than active bug; relates to CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes on canonical helpers
fix_summary: Export FamilyRHEL and FamilyDebian from internal/platform and use the constants at the three sites. Also expose a DefaultOS() helper so the fallback is not assembled inline (the "rhel default" assumption appears twice).

smell: Two functions build a display status string via the same switch on (Skipped/Success/default) producing the literal values "skip"/"ok"/"fail". The value set is a three-state enum spelled inline in two places; adding a fourth state (e.g. "partial") would require editing both.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: duplicated 3-way switch producing stringly-typed output across two functions within the same file
fix_summary: Introduce a StepResult.DisplayStatus() method returning a typed StatusLabel (or even a plain stepStatus enum with a String() method) so callers write `sb.kv(string(s.StepID), fmt.Sprintf("%-4s  %s", s.DisplayStatus(), d))` once. Or hoist the switch into a local helper in summary.go.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §code-comments (rubric favoring extraction when switch repeats)
Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: 26 sites across cleanup/ (and one in setup/phase.go) guard every log call with `if logger != nil { logger.Info(...) }` instead of accepting a guaranteed-non-nil *slog.Logger. CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes names logutil.NopLogger as the canonical no-op fallback precisely for this case; adopting it at constructors would delete 26 branches and make the call sites read as plain Go.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: canonical helper (logutil.NopLogger) is bypassed at 26 sites — cosmetic but CLAUDE.md-named
fix_summary: Add a small `logger := cmp.Or(loggerArg, logutil.NopLogger)` (or a defaultLogger helper) at the top of each Cleanup/Setup function, then drop the 26 `if logger != nil {` guards and the 4 `else if logger != nil {` branches. Matches the pattern already in use at internal/distribution/okd/cleanup/cleanup.go:37-42 (getLogger method).
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: 'internal/logutil.NopLogger is the canonical no-op logger. Don't write slog.New(slog.DiscardHandler) inline.'

smell: Package `packages` wraps `platform.PackageManager.Install`/`Remove` with an extra logger.Info() envelope and a single `fmt.Errorf` rewrap. Three call sites consume it (two in cleanup/, one in setup/), none of which need a distinct package — the value added is two log lines that could be written inline. This is a one-function-per-verb package with 40 LOC total.
fix_summary: Inline the two functions at their three call sites (setup/steps.go:294, cleanup/packages.go:59, cleanup/services.go:38) and delete internal/distribution/okd/packages. The logger.Info lines are already repeated in the callers' surrounding context. Or keep only one helper if a future 4th caller is imminent.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: canonical helpers list (packages not listed)
Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: CSR.Pending is a boolean field that is unconditionally set to `true` by its only constructor (cluster.PendingCSRs) and never read anywhere. It is named to suggest tri-state (Pending/Approved/Denied) but the producer only emits Pending rows. Either the field is dead, or the CSR type should grow to carry the full conditions slice.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: field has no downstream reader and conveys no information — removing it is a one-line drop but the type is exported, so a consumer edit may be required
fix_summary: Delete the `Pending bool` field and the `Pending: true` assignment. The type name and constructor already convey that every returned CSR is pending. If a future consumer needs to distinguish states, introduce a CSRState enum (Pending/Approved/Denied) rather than a bool.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: AddonInfo.Category is populated by the two catalog addons ("gitops", "secrets") but is not read anywhere in the codebase. It is a stringly-typed metadata field reserved for a future grouping UI. If that UI is on the roadmap, keep it as scaffolding; if not, it is dead weight encouraging ad-hoc values.
fix_summary: Verify intent against roadmap.md. If a category-grouped wizard/list is planned, keep the field and add a typed AddonCategory enum (gitops/secrets/storage/…) so callers can't typo "gitops " or "git-ops". If not, drop the field.

smell: addon.IsRegistered has no callers. However it is a clean symmetric API pair with Register/Get (if Register exists, IsRegistered stays by symmetric-API rubric). Flag as scaffolding rather than dead code.
fix_summary: Keep. Verify against roadmap.md — if addon CLI subcommands (`okdctl addon list`, `okdctl addon info <name>`) are planned, this is the primitive they need; otherwise consider collapsing to `addon.Get(name) != nil` at the one future caller.

smell: LogLevel is a custom enum (Debug/Info/Warn/Error) that is not referenced anywhere — the package exposes Debug()/Info()/Warn()/Error() functions directly and uses charmlog.Level for level parsing. The enum is a premature abstraction that shadows log/slog's own leveling.
evidence:
type LogLevel int

const (
    LogLevelDebug LogLevel = iota
    LogLevelInfo
    LogLevelWarn
    LogLevelError
)
fix_summary: Delete the LogLevel type and its four constants. Callers wanting a typed level should import log/slog.Level directly (LevelDebug/LevelInfo/LevelWarn/LevelError) — that's also the seam audit-modernization will push toward.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: retrieveProvisionResult hardcodes the VM name literals "bootstrap", and uses Sprintf patterns `"master%d"` / `"worker%d"` for the other roles. The role *values* ARE typed (RoleBootstrap/RoleMaster/RoleWorker), but the *names* duplicate the string — so `Name: "bootstrap"` and `Role: RoleBootstrap` sit side by side and can drift. setup/nodes.go repeats the pattern.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: Name and Role are parallel stringly-typed channels; rename one and they diverge silently
fix_summary: Use the role constant as the name prefix: `Name: fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", RoleMaster, i)` and `Name: string(RoleBootstrap)`. Or add a VMRole.NodeName(index int) helper so the single-source-of-truth is the VMRole type.

smell: Default CPU type is the bare literal "host" with no named constant. The surrounding file has 50-default-gb and "virtio" literals as well (lines 33, 121); together they form a small cluster of config-shaped defaults that belong in a `defaults` block alongside Topology/Networking.
fix_summary: Define `const DefaultProxmoxCPUType = "host"` (and similarly DefaultNetworkModel = "virtio", DefaultOSDiskGB = 50) either in terraform.go or in an internal/config/defaults.go extension, and reference the constant. Matches the existing constant block at internal/config/constants.go.

smell: Manager.IsInstalled uses a bespoke `queryMatch` string substring to distinguish "installed" from "purged" on dpkg output. The logic is correct but the two-branch design (empty → exit-code-only, non-empty → substring match) is a mini-DSL inside a single method. Splitting into two tiny methods (isInstalledRHEL/isInstalledDebian) or delegating to a per-family func field would read more plainly.
fix_summary: Replace the `queryMatch` string field with `postCheck func(stdout []byte, pkg string) bool` on Manager. Set it to a no-op in the RHEL constructor and a dpkg-ii-prefix check in the Debian constructor. Method body becomes `return m.postCheck(output, pkg)`.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: Four constructors implement the same nil-guard setter idiom `func(x *T) { if l != nil { x.logger = l } }` with the stated contract 'keeps the existing noop logger if nil'. Good defensive style per site, but the pattern is stamped in four places without a shared helper. A small `logutil.OrNop(l)` or similar would centralize the policy the CLAUDE.md canonical-helper note already names.
fix_summary: Add `func OrNop(l *slog.Logger) *slog.Logger { if l == nil { return NopLogger }; return l }` to internal/logutil, and rewrite the four constructors as `c.logger = logutil.OrNop(l)`. Saves 12 LOC and makes the pattern grep-findable.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: 'internal/logutil.NopLogger is the canonical no-op logger.'
Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: getDiskSizes returns `(cpDisk, workerDisk, workerDataDisk, masterDataDisk int)` — four unnamed integers with no semantic ordering. The named returns do document the positional identity, but the real signal a caller needs is 'which is which'. A struct (or four explicit calls) would be safer; the current shape is a 4-int tuple begging for a mis-reordering bug.
fix_summary: Replace the 4-int tuple with a `type diskSizes struct { cpOS, workerOS, workerData, masterData int }` and return the struct. The single caller (buildTerraformVarsData) then assigns by field name, not by position.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever

smell: OKDVersion.Major() and OKDVersion.Minor() parse the Version string via fmt.Sscanf on every call. Callers use them inside filter loops (cli/releases.go, tui/wizard/steps/distribution.go), so a list of 40 releases does ~80 Sscanf parses per display even though the version string is immutable per OKDVersion.
fix_summary: Parse once at unmarshal time (or memoize). Either (a) add unexported `major, minor int` fields and populate them in the fetcher's parseVersion flow, or (b) use `strings.Cut(v.Version, ".")` + strconv.Atoi, which is 5x faster and avoids the fmt machinery. Sscanf is overkill for two integers.
rule_source: Uber §Avoid String Concatenation in Loops (analogue: avoid fmt in loops)

smell: The if/else-if/else ladder around token assembly has an `else if px.TokenID != ""` branch whose `if` branch explicitly does nothing (`_ = px.TokenID`). The comment explains the semantic (avoid "tokenid=tokenid=secret" double-prefix), but the empty-but-for-a-side-channel branch is an anti-pattern — invert the condition and return early, or drop the branch if the semantic is already covered by the else-if.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: semantic is correct but the shape (empty-then-else) is the kind of thing linters flag when they pick up the idiom
fix_summary: Collapse to: `if px.TokenID != "" && !strings.Contains(px.APIToken, "=") { token = px.TokenID + "=" + px.APIToken }`. Same behavior, no empty branch, no `_ = px.TokenID` dummy to confuse future readers.
